title: Kernel sweep microbench results (seq len × batch × KV cache) — Feb 2026
content:
Purpose
- Microbench sweeps to explain macro benchmark movements seen in Q1 2026 baseline Run 1 (notably long-context + streaming tail, and a couple of throughput dips under mid-sized batches).
- Used by kernels team to answer: “Is this regression coming from kernel selection, from scheduler, or from KV cache behavior?”

TL;DR (what changed / what we think is happening)
1) Long-context prefill (seq >= 8k) shows a clear bifurcation between two attention kernel families.
   - When kernel auto-selection picks K_attn_v3_ws (workspace-heavy variant), prefill time increases 10–25% depending on batch and causes downstream queueing → p95/p99 in macro suite.
   - The selection is sensitive to minor runtime differences (autotune jitter, driver patch, available workspace).
   - This matches the “regression only for long-context streaming” symptom from Slack thread 1708444444.

2) Decode tokens/sec is mostly stable across kernels for short seq, but for seq >= 8k and batch >= 8 we see a 6–12% drop when KV cache compaction triggers frequently.
   - This correlates with spikes in KV cache compaction counters (see PR-24077 notes). The effect is stronger on A100 vs H100.

3) Determinism/pinning helps: reruns using the pinned kernel selection logic (PR-23877) eliminate run-to-run drift in the long-context region and reduce variance enough to fit the variance budget targets (Sana’s draft budgets).

If you only read one table: see “Sweep summary (H100) — long-context prefill” below.

Environment / setup
- Harness: benchmark-lab sweep runner (post PR-419 traffic generator; microbench mode)
- Runtime build: redwood runtime @ approx Feb 2026 (see commit refs below)
- Model used for microbench: Llama-3.1-70B (BF16) and Llama-3.1-8B for sanity checks
  - Note: exact model weights don’t matter much for the relative kernel comparison, but absolute numbers do.
- Hardware:
  - H100 SXM 80GB (primary)
  - A100 80GB (secondary)
- CUDA/Driver:
  - H100: CUDA 12.4, driver 550.54.14 (pinned in runner)
  - A100: CUDA 12.2, driver 545.23.08 (pinned in runner)
- Clocks/Power: application clocks pinned; persistence mode enabled
- Process isolation: single tenant on the node; no colocated jobs; NUMA pinned
- Batch definition:
  - “batch” = number of concurrent sequences in a continuous-batching window (microbench enforces fixed batch per step)
- KV cache conditions:
  - cold: no prefix reuse; kv cache starts empty
  - warm: prefix reuse enabled; 90% prefix match over the first N tokens (see “KV scenarios”)
- Metrics reported:
  - Prefill_ms (end-to-end prefill for the request)
  - Decode_tps (tokens/sec during decode steady-state; averaged over 128 decoded tokens unless otherwise noted)
  - Kernel_time_ms (CUDA kernel time for attention op only, from NVTX range)
  - H2D/D2H excluded (microbench uses in-process tensors)

Commit references / variants compared
- Variant A (baseline): runtime before kernel pinning change (auto-select may vary)
  - ref: redwood @ pre PR-23877 (exact SHA recorded in artifact metadata)
- Variant B (pinned): runtime with deterministic kernel selection/pinning
  - ref: includes github:redwood/pr-23877
- Variant C (cache counters): runtime with KV cache compaction counter refactor (for visibility)
  - ref: includes github:redwood/pr-24077

Data location
- Artifact bundle: gs://redwood-benchmark-artifacts/microbench/kernel_sweep/2026-02/
  - H100: …/h100_sxm80/
  - A100: …/a100_80g/
- Each run includes:
  - config.yaml, environment.json, nvtx_ranges.json, summary.csv, raw_samples.csv

KV scenarios (microbench)
- KV0 (cold): cache_hit=0%, prefix_len=0
- KV50 (mixed): cache_hit=50%, prefix_len=1024
- KV90 (warm): cache_hit=90%, prefix_len=2048


Sweep 1: Sequence length × batch size (H100, KV0/cold)
Model: Llama-3.1-70B BF16
Output length fixed: 256 decode tokens

Sweep summary (H100) — long-context prefill (most relevant to macro suite tail)
- Prefill_ms shown as p50 over 30 trials (microbench is stable when pinned)

| seq_len | batch | Variant A Prefill_ms | Variant B Prefill_ms | Delta (B vs A) | Notes |
|--------:|------:|---------------------:|---------------------:|---------------:|------|
| 2048    | 1     | 118                  | 117                  | -0.8%          | no meaningful diff |
| 2048    | 8     | 142                  | 141                  | -0.7%          | stable |
| 8192    | 1     | 472                  | 441                  | -6.6%          | A sometimes picks ws-heavy kernel |
| 8192    | 4     | 596                  | 528                  | -11.4%         | biggest improvement in region we care about |
| 8192    | 8     | 742                  | 612                  | -17.5%         | A exhibits higher jitter across trials |
| 16384   | 1     | 960                  | 872                  | -9.2%          | workspace pressure starts to matter |
| 16384   | 4     | 1310                 | 1108                 | -15.4%         | A shows occasional outliers (spill) |
| 16384   | 8     | 1715                 | 1412                 | -17.7%         | aligns w/ macro regression shape |

Interpretation
- When the auto-selector lands on the workspace-heavy kernel (K_attn_v3_ws), H100 prefill grows materially at seq>=8k and batch>=4.
- In macro suite, this shows up as higher queue wait + p95/p99, especially for streaming (because TTFT amplifies prefill delay and streaming requests hold connections longer).
- Pinning (Variant B) forces K_attn_v3_smallws (or equivalent) in this region and removes the cliff.


Sweep 2: Decode throughput (H100, KV0/cold)
Same model/workload, focusing on decode tokens/sec.

| seq_len | batch | Variant A Decode_tps | Variant B Decode_tps | Delta | Notes |
|--------:|------:|---------------------:|---------------------:|------:|------|
| 2048    | 1     | 245                  | 244                  | -0.4% | decode largely unchanged |
| 2048    | 8     | 1270                 | 1268                 | -0.2% | |
| 8192    | 1     | 212                  | 213                  | +0.5% | |
| 8192    | 8     | 1035                 | 1042                 | +0.7% | small win (better prefill overlap) |
| 16384   | 4     | 756                  | 761                  | +0.7% | |

Interpretation
- Decode is not the main culprit for the macro movement we’re investigating (it’s prefill-driven in this case).


Sweep 3: KV cache scenarios (H100)
Goal: check whether warm-prefix reuse changes which kernel variant wins, and whether cache compaction is interacting with attention.

Model: Llama-3.1-70B BF16
Fixed: seq_len=8192, output=256

| KV scenario | batch | Prefill_ms (Variant B) | Decode_tps (Variant B) | Observations |
|-----------:|------:|------------------------:|------------------------:|-------------|
| KV0        | 4     | 528                     | 918                     | baseline |
| KV50       | 4     | 401                     | 910                     | prefill improves as expected |
| KV90       | 4     | 352                     | 906                     | diminishing returns past 50% |
| KV0        | 8     | 612                     | 1042                    | baseline |
| KV50       | 8     | 468                     | 1031                    | |
| KV90       | 8     | 421                     | 1025                    | |

Interpretation
- Warm-prefix reuse reduces prefill time materially (expected).
- The kernel cliff we saw in Variant A is still present when KV reuse is enabled, but is harder to notice because the absolute prefill budget is smaller.
- Recommendation: keep pinned selection regardless of KV state; do not rely on “warm cache hides it”.


Sweep 4: A100 comparison (sanity + why one region looked noisier)
Model: Llama-3.1-70B BF16
Caveat: absolute numbers not directly comparable to H100.

Long-context prefill (A100, KV0)

| seq_len | batch | Variant A Prefill_ms | Variant B Prefill_ms | Delta | Notes |
|--------:|------:|---------------------:|---------------------:|------:|------|
| 8192    | 4     | 1048                 | 1002                | -4.4% | smaller win than H100 |
| 8192    | 8     | 1380                 | 1265                | -8.3% | A100 more sensitive to workspace |
| 16384   | 4     | 2245                 | 2031                | -9.5% | |

Observations
- A100 exhibits more variance if other processes touch GPU memory (even small). Our isolation settings reduced this but didn’t eliminate it fully.
- This supports the hypothesis from baseline variance thread 1706123456 that some of the “region noise” was actually fleet-mix + driver drift + memory pressure.


Kernel-level notes (from NVTX ranges + profiler snapshots)
- The regression signature for Variant A runs that are slow:
  - attention kernel time increases disproportionately vs matmul/MLP
  - increased L2 misses + occasional local memory spills
  - workspace allocation pattern differs (suspect allocator fragmentation or different kernel requiring larger scratch)

- Variant B (pinned) runs:
  - stable attention kernel selection
  - reduced scratch
  - consistent kernel launch sequence


Cross-reference to macro suite anomalies
- Baseline Run 1 anomaly: “regression only for long-context streaming” (Slack 1708444444)
  - Microbench reproduces the kernel cliff at seq>=8k, batch>=4.
  - Streaming magnifies the user-visible impact via TTFT + held-open connections; scheduler then compounds queueing.

- Scheduler fix PR-23981 may hide symptoms but doesn’t remove the kernel cliff.
  - We should treat kernel pinning (PR-23877) as primary prevention, scheduler changes as tail-risk mitigation.


Recommendations / next actions
1) Treat pinned/deterministic kernel selection as baseline-critical (already in PR-23877)
   - Action: ensure runner records the exact kernel IDs used per sweep; include in microbench summary output.
   - Owner: Yuki / Grace

2) Add a microbench gate to perf smoke for “seq=8192 batch=8 prefill_ms” and “seq=16384 batch=4 prefill_ms”
   - Not as a hard fail initially; warn-only to catch a return of the cliff.
   - Owner: Marcus / Sahana (ties into github:redwood/pr-23905 direction)

3) KV cache compaction interaction: quantify impact under decode-heavy workloads
   - We only did output=256. Need output=2048 variant to see steady-state decode + compaction effects.
   - Owner: Omar / Samir

4) Fleet normalization: we need a tiny “kernel fingerprint” to detect if driver/CUDA drift changes selection behavior
   - Suggest: at runner start, run seq=4096 batch=4 microbench and record selected kernel + kernel_time_ms.
   - Owner: Vanessa / Grace

Open questions
- Are we relying on allocator state too much? Would a per-run “allocator defrag” (or prealloc pool) help ensure stable workspace availability?
- Do we want the selector to consider “streaming TTFT sensitivity” explicitly (prefer kernels with predictable prefill even if slightly slower median)?
- Is the A100 variance acceptable within Sana’s variance budgets, or do we need stricter node isolation for A100 regions?

Appendix A: Exact sweep grid
- seq_len: 128, 512, 2048, 8192, 16384
- batch: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16
- KV scenarios: KV0, KV50, KV90
- trials per cell: 30 (after 10 warmup iterations)

Appendix B: Notes from the week
- 2026-02-12: first pass sweep; saw cliff at 8k/16k; suspected scheduler—microbench isolated to prefill attention.
- 2026-02-14: reran with pinned environment; cliff persisted only when kernel selection varied.
- 2026-02-16: added kernel ID logging; confirmed different kernel family chosen in slow trials.
- 2026-02-19: A100 verification; variance higher; suspect driver + memory pressure sensitivity.
